standard_prerequisites.name: Localization at a multiplicative system
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter and Categories, the construction of the localization and the universal property of the localization functor
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the functor Q and the fact that it carries the morphisms of the multiplicative system to isomorphisms.

standard_prerequisites.name: Which morphisms the localization inverts
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the criterion that a morphism becomes an isomorphism in the localization exactly when it can be completed to an element of the multiplicative system, which produces condition (3) from condition (1).

core_obligations: (2) implies (1) and (3) implies (1) (proof lines 2116-2118): if the zero morphism from X to some object belongs to the system, its image under Q is an isomorphism, which in an additive category forces Q(X) to be zero; the same argument applies to the zero morphism into X.

(1) implies (3) (proof lines 2119-2124): if Q(X) is zero then the zero morphism into X becomes an isomorphism, so the cited criterion produces a morphism out of X whose composite with the zero morphism lies in the system, which is condition (3).
(1) implies (2) (proof line 2125): the same argument, applied in the other direction, gives the remaining implication.
proof_roadmap: Show that a zero morphism in the multiplicative system forces the localized object to vanish.
Use the criterion for inverted morphisms to produce an element of the system from the vanishing of the localized object.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes the objects that the localization functor at a multiplicative system sends to zero, by the existence of a zero morphism into or out of the object that belongs to the multiplicative system (statement lines 2101-2113). The proof is a complete argument: two of the implications follow because the localized image of an element of the system is an isomorphism and an additive category has no nontrivial isomorphism on a zero object (proof lines 2116-2118); the remaining ones use the criterion describing which morphisms become invertible to produce an element of the system from the vanishing of the localized object (proof lines 2119-2124 and 2125). The non-formal content is the application of the inversion criterion. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
